## What I did and did not do

I did not run any pull. Every figure below comes from what you supplied, and it is labelled that way. No new sources were fetched.

Two things constrain the brief before it starts:

- **The volume is Australia-only.** 900/mo AU for August 2026 is not a global figure and must never be quoted as one. AU is a small share of English-language search for a Mac-only productivity app, so the global number is likely several times larger , but "likely" is not a number, so the cell says AU.
- **Exact prompt volume is unavailable.** The vendor's Phrase 400 does not go in the number column. Phrase absorbs any-order matches on a four-word term ("windows", "things", "3" are all high-frequency tokens), so 400 would promote this topic on a figure that partly describes unrelated queries. The cell reads "No data".

---

## Numbers table (evidence)

| Keyword | Search volume | Exact prompt volume | Source, scope, window |
|---|---|---|---|
| things 3 for windows | 900 | No data | Supplied export, Australia, monthly for August 2026, received 2026-09-08 |
| Phrase-match prompt figure (not recorded as volume) | , | Not used | Vendor offered Phrase 400; Exact unavailable, so no prompt volume is recorded |
| Secondary candidates (things 3 windows alternative, things 3 alternative for pc, apps like things 3 for windows) | No data | No data | Not in the supplied export; no pull authorised |
| Brand search volume (your product) | No data | No data | Not supplied; not pulled |

No modifier added to the primary. "things 3 for windows" is already intent-specific , the searcher wants a Windows version of a specific app , and forcing a modifier on it would only shrink an already-precise query.

---

## Brief

```markdown
# Brief: Things 3 for Windows

Date: 2026-09-08  ·  Status: Request

## Why this page exists

Audience: Things 3 users on Mac/iOS who have moved to, or added, a Windows machine and
are searching for a Windows version before deciding whether to stay or switch.
Gap: The query has a high-intent, disappointing answer. Searchers land on forum threads
and roundup listicles, not on one page that states the platform situation plainly and
then explains what switching actually costs them.
Job of the page: decide

## SEO decisions

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Primary keyword | things 3 for windows |
| Search volume | 900 (supplied export, Australia, monthly, August 2026) , AU only, not global |
| Exact prompt volume | No data (vendor Exact unavailable; Phrase figure deliberately not recorded) |
| Secondary keywords | things 3 windows alternative (No data), apps like things 3 for windows (No data) , volumes required before these shape the page |
| Title | Things 3 for Windows: what your options actually are |
| H1 | Things 3 for Windows: what your options actually are |
| Meta description | Things 3 runs on Apple platforms; here is what that means if you work on Windows, and how to decide between waiting, splitting tools, or moving. |
| Canonical | <site>/things-3-for-windows , confirm final path and host before publish |

## North star

Tone: level and unpromotional. The reader has just been told "no" by a search result;
a page that opens with a pitch loses them in one scroll.
The reader should leave knowing: whether to keep Things and work around Windows, or move,
and what the move costs them in practice.

## Ideas to land

- Answer the platform question in the first two sentences, before any framing.
- The real decision is not "which app is best" but "what happens to my existing system":
  projects, areas, tags, repeating to-dos, and years of completed history.
- Name what is genuinely lost in any move away from Things, not only what is gained.
  A page that admits the cost is the one that gets trusted and cited.
- Cross-platform is the whole reason this query exists; treat it as the deciding
  criterion, not as a feature bullet.

Not an outline. The writer sets order and section breaks.

## Shape

Problem → evidence → questions → how to do it → short close.

## Questions worth answering

Evaluator questions first.

1. Is there a Things 3 app for Windows?
2. Will Things 3 ever come to Windows?
3. Can I use Things 3 in a browser on a PC?
4. What do people use instead of Things 3 on Windows?
5. What does Things 3 do that other task apps don't?
6. Can I export my Things 3 data, and what comes out?
7. Is it worth keeping a Mac just for Things?
8. How do I move Things projects and areas into another app?
9. What breaks when I switch task managers?
10. [Product-specific] Does <product> run on Windows, and how does it handle a Things-style
    projects-and-areas setup?

Cluster note: an AI surface answering "things 3 for windows" will fan out to roughly
questions 1, 2, 4, and 6 concurrently. Cover all four somewhere on the site, not one
narrow page aimed at the single string.

## Sources the writer can cite

- Cultured Code's official Things product and support pages (writer to confirm live URLs
  and current platform statements at time of writing)
- Cultured Code's public FAQ or support article on Windows/PC support, if one exists
- Your own public product page and public docs for the Windows claim

Public product pages, public docs, and published research only. Do not cite forum posts
as statements of vendor intent.
```

---

## Things the writer must not be handed as fact

- **Your product name and Windows details.** You told me the product works on Windows; you did not tell me its name, its platform list beyond that, or how it imports Things data. I have left `<product>` and the canonical path as placeholders rather than inventing them. Fill both before handover.
- **Any claim about Cultured Code's roadmap.** The page can state what the vendor publicly says today, with a date beside it. It cannot state that Windows "will never" ship. Anything the writer cannot verify on a public Cultured Code page gets cut.
- **An import/migration claim.** If your product cannot import Things data, the brief's idea about "what happens to my existing system" must be honest about that. Confirm before the writer starts.

---

## Recommended next evidence, in priority order

1. **Global and US volume for the primary.** The whole prioritisation rests on 900 AU/mo. If global is 8,000 this is a flagship page; if global is 1,400 it is a modest one. One pull, same window, scope recorded.
2. **Volumes for the two secondary candidates.** Without them the writer cannot judge whether "alternative"-shaped queries deserve their own H2s or their own page. Right now they are themes with no numbers, which is exactly the failure mode that gets a page written on vibes.
3. **Exact prompt volume, re-attempted.** If Exact stays empty next window, record "No data" again permanently rather than substituting Phrase. Worth one retry because a query phrased as a yes/no platform question is a natural chat prompt.
4. **Your brand search volume.** It is the strongest published predictor of AI-search visibility in Ahrefs' 75,000-brand study (0.392, versus 0.218 for backlinks), and it is the one number on this brief that this page will not move. Note it is not the top correlate , branded web mentions (0.664) and YouTube mentions (0.737) both beat it , so record which of the three you measured rather than calling it "the" predictor.
5. **Search Console query report**, if the site has any traffic. Keyword-tool related-keyword databases are usually thin for a competitor-name seed like this one; GSC is the real related-query universe for your own domain.

## Metrics to report on, once the page ships

Report state changes, not state. For this page specifically: clicks and impressions for the primary and its variants at 28-day-over-28-day, average position on the primary, and whether the page appears in the AI surfaces , tracked per engine, named individually, never pooled into one "AI visibility" number. ChatGPT and Perplexity overlap on roughly a tenth of cited domains, so a blended figure would describe neither.

I have not created a monitoring schedule and none is running. Say the word if you want one proposed against whatever scheduler and Search Console access you actually have connected.
